t: Sho Hashi unified Okinawa in 1429 and ruled from Shuri as a tributary king of Ming China.
Royal ships carried Chinese, Japanese and Southeast Asian goods, making Ryukyu a major trading hub in the 15th and 16th centuries.
After Satsuma's invasion in 1609 it served China and Japan at once, until Meiji Japan annexed it as Okinawa Prefecture.
dyk: The bronze bell cast for Shuri Castle in 1458 bears an inscription calling Ryukyu a 'bridge of all nations', linking China, Japan and Korea by its ships.
ev: Sho Hashi conquers Nanzan and completes the unification of Okinawa
The 'bridge of all nations' bell is cast for Shuri Castle
Kanemaru takes the throne as Sho En, founding the Second Sho dynasty
Sho Shin's forces defeat Oyake Akahachi and take control of the Yaeyama Islands
Satsuma invades and King Sho Nei surrenders Shuri
Tamagusuku Chokun's kumi odori dance-dramas are first performed for Chinese envoys
Commodore Perry signs a compact with the kingdom at Naha
Japan abolishes the Ryukyu Domain and creates Okinawa Prefecture
